prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The allowance for credit losses totaled $125.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $77.2 million as of December 31, 2025. Our allowance for credit losses at September 30, 2026 was 1.04% of total loans, compared to 0.89% at December 31, 2025. The $48.4 million increase in our allowance for credit losses from December 31, 2025 reflected the initial ACL of $46.6 million on the purchased credit deteriorated (“PCD”) loans and purchased seasoned loans (“PSL”) acquired in the Heritage acquisition as well as a provision for credit losses of $2.0 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Net charge-offs were $148,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net recoveries of $214,000 for the same period last year.

The allowance for credit losses as of September 30, 2026 is based upon lifetime loss rate models developed from an estimation framework that uses historical lifetime loss experiences to derive loss rates at a collective pool level. We measure the expected credit losses on a collective (pooled) basis for those loans that share similar risk characteristics. We have three collective loan pools: Commercial Real Estate, Commercial and Industrial, and Consumer. Our ACL amounts are largely driven by portfolio characteristics, including loss history and various risk attributes, and the economic outlook for certain macroeconomic variables.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The Company’s effective tax rate for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 26.38% and 26.00%, respectively, compared with 23.80% and 25.60% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Our estimated annual effective tax rate also varies depending upon the level of tax-advantaged income from municipal securities and BOLI, as well as available tax credits.

The Company’s effective tax rates are below the nominal combined Federal and State tax rate primarily as a result of tax-advantaged income from certain municipal security investments, municipal loans and leases and BOLI, as well as available tax credits for each period.

ocf.text: The objective of liquidity management is to ensure that funds are available in a timely manner to meet our financial obligations when they come due without incurring unnecessary cost or risk, or causing a disruption to our normal operating activities. This includes the ability to manage unplanned decreases or changes in funding sources, accommodate loan demand and growth, fund investments, repurchase securities, pay creditors as necessary, and meet other operating or capital needs.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text: The principal component of our earnings is net interest income, which is the difference between the interest and fees earned on loans and investments (interest-earning assets) and the interest paid on deposits and borrowed funds (interest-bearing liabilities). Net interest margin is net interest income as a percentage of average interest-earning assets for the period. The level of interest rates and the volume and mix of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities impact net interest income and net interest margin. The net interest spread is the yield on average interest-earning assets minus the cost of average interest-bearing liabilities. Net interest margin and net interest spread are included on a tax-equivalent (“TE”) basis by adjusting interest income utilizing the federal statutory corporate tax rates of 21% in effect for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. Our net interest income, interest spread, and net interest margin are sensitive to general business and economic conditions. These conditions include short-term and long-term interest rates, inflation, monetary supply, and the strength of the international, national and state economies, in general, and more specifically, the local economies in which we conduct business.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income includes income derived from financial services offered to our customers, such as CitizensTrust, merchant processing and card services, international banking, and other business services. Also included in noninterest income are service charges and fees, primarily from deposit accounts, gains (net of losses) from the disposition of investment securities, loans, other real estate owned, and fixed assets, and other revenues not included as interest on earning assets.

intro.text: CVB Financial Corp. (referred to herein on an unconsolidated basis as “CVB” and on a consolidated basis as “we”, “our” or the “Company”) is a bank holding company incorporated in California on April 27, 1981 and registered with the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (“Federal Reserve”) under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the “BHCA”). The Company commenced business on December 30, 1981 when, pursuant to a reorganization, it acquired all of the voting stock of Chino Valley Bank. On March 29, 1996, Chino Valley Bank changed its name to Citizens Business Bank, and on December 15, 2025, Citizens Business Bank changed its name to Citizens Business Bank, National Association (“CBB” or the “Bank”). The Bank is our principal asset. The Company has one inactive subsidiary, Chino Valley Bancorp.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
